title: Campaign: non-invasive brain measurement, coupled methods: one energy modulates another
abstract: Subcampaign of 'how can human brain activity be measured without surgery, better than today?'. Scope: Methods in which one form of energy marks or modulates another before detection: photoacoustics (light in, sound out), ultrasound-tagged light, acoustoelectric imaging, ultrasound-tagged electrical recording, and MR or ultrasound elastography. 55 papers. Status: confounds dominate, with one narrow gain. In simulated transcranial photoacoustics the signal is dominated by scalp (median scalp/brain ratio 56 in one calibrated model; 85-96% of apparent-brain voxel signal in another; cortical changes diluted to a few percent). With continuous ultrasound tagging 61-99% of tagged light comes from scalp, but gated pulsed tagging takes 33-72% from cortex under the beam. In a four-shell sphere model, scalp acoustoelectric imaging needs about 40 minutes to 9 hours of activity per 1.6 mm voxel (about tenfold uncertainty). Reported functional MR elastography effects need 13-35% intrinsic stiffening against an estimated 3.7-13%, and same-run voxel selection inflates means 1.6-5x.
